steps.stdout:
Mark a task a session was working on as no longer held.

Without --task or --session, the task in this session's attachment is
closed: the one a plain `session attach` took, and the one whose
attachment file is then removed. With --task, that task is closed
instead, as slug#number (the form `session status` prints), a number,
or an id. A bare number names the held task when the attachment
carries its project — it wins over the current project's task of
that number — and is read in the current project otherwise. That
releases one of several a session may hold. The attachment is only
removed when it is that task, so a session attached elsewhere stays
attached there, and a task this session attached earlier can be
closed with no attachment at all.

With --session <id>, the hold of another session is released instead:
a closed marker is posted for that session id on the task --task names.
This is the way to let go of a session whose host can no longer run the
close itself — an imported board can carry markers for hosts that are
gone — since nothing on this machine records that session.

Usage:
  kaneo session close [--task <task>] [--session <id>] [flags]

Flags:
      --allow-archived   write to the resolved project even though it is archived
  -h, --help             help for close
      --session string   release another session's hold on --task, by session id
      --strict           report failures instead of exiting quietly; this command is otherwise silent on error so it is safe to call from a hook
      --task string      task to close, as slug#number, number or id; required with --session

Global Flags:
      --api-key string     API key; prefer KANEO_API_KEY, since a flag is visible in the process list
      --api-url string     Kaneo base URL (env KANEO_API_URL)
      --human              force human-readable output, even through a pipe
      --jq string          filter JSON output with a jq expression (implies --json)
      --json               force JSON output
  -p, --project string     project id, slug or name (env KANEO_PROJECT)
      --timeout duration   timeout for each request and each --jq evaluation (default 10s)
  -w, --workspace string   workspace id, slug or name (env KANEO_WORKSPACE)
